title: TOEIC Listening and Reading
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public TOEIC test specifications. Not a capture of past test questions.

items.stem: A photograph shows a woman at a service counter handing a document to a clerk while a line of customers waits behind her. What is the woman doing?
options: Signing a contract at a desk
Handing a document to a clerk
Paying for groceries at a till
items.explanation: The photograph places the woman at the counter passing a document to the clerk, which matches the option about handing over a document; the other options show actions the image does not support.

items.stem: In a photograph, three colleagues stand around a whiteboard covered in coloured charts while one of them points at a graph. What are the people doing?
items.explanation: The scene shows a group gathered at a whiteboard of charts with one person pointing, so they are reviewing charts; the other options describe unrelated activities.

items.stem: In a short exchange, a voice asks, "Where should I leave the delivery boxes?" Which response is the most appropriate reply?
options: I left my phone at home.
items.explanation: The question asks for a location, so the reply naming the loading dock answers it; the others give a yes or no, an unrelated statement, or a comment on weight.

items.stem: A caller asks, "Could you send me the sales figures by Friday?" Which response would a colleague most likely give?
options: Friday is a busy day for sales.
Of course, I will email them this afternoon.
I have never met the sales team.
items.explanation: The request is for the figures by Friday, so a promise to email them answers it directly; the other replies do not respond to the request.

items.stem: A customer says, "I would like to change the date of my reservation." Which reply is the most appropriate?
options: Certainly. What date would you prefer?
No, I do not work here.
items.explanation: A date change requires asking for the new date, so that reply is appropriate; the others ignore the request or are irrelevant.

items.stem: An interviewer asks, "How long have you worked in customer service?" Which answer best fits the question?
options: For about six years, mostly in retail.
I parked in the visitor lot.
Yes, the interview room is upstairs.
items.explanation: The question asks about duration of experience, so a response giving years in the field fits; the others answer questions that were not asked.

items.stem: In a conversation, a manager says the quarterly report is due Thursday, and an employee replies that two supplier invoices are still missing. What is the employee's concern?
options: The manager forgot to attend a meeting
The employee wants a longer holiday
Some information needed for the report is not yet available
items.explanation: The employee points to missing invoices, which are inputs to the report, so the concern is that required information is still outstanding.

items.stem: In a conversation, a customer calls to say a laptop ordered last week has not arrived, and the agent offers to trace the shipment and call back within an hour. What will the agent do?
options: Track the shipment and telephone the customer back
Ask the customer to visit the store
items.explanation: The agent promises to trace the shipment and call back, so that is the step to be taken; the other options are not offered.

items.stem: In a conversation at a hotel front desk, a guest asks whether a meeting room is free on Tuesday morning for eight people. What does the guest want?
options: To reserve a meeting room for a small group
To hire a car for the day
To complain about a noisy room
items.explanation: The guest asks about a room's availability for eight people, meaning they want to reserve a small meeting room, not travel or complain.

items.stem: In a conversation, a supervisor tells a new employee that the warehouse uses a barcode scanner for every item and shows where the device is kept. What is the supervisor doing?
options: Explaining a work procedure to a new employee
items.explanation: The supervisor describes a recurring work method and where equipment is kept, which is explaining a procedure to someone new.

items.stem: An announcement states, "Attention shoppers, the store will close in fifteen minutes. Please bring your purchases to the checkout on the ground floor." What are shoppers asked to do?
options: Leave the building immediately without paying
Take their purchases to the ground-floor checkout
Collect a free gift from the entrance
Return to the store tomorrow morning
items.explanation: The announcement asks shoppers to bring purchases to the ground-floor checkout before closing; it does not mention leaving unpaid or gifts.

items.stem: An announcement states, "The 9.15 express to Central Station is delayed by twenty minutes due to track maintenance." What does the announcement say about the train?
options: It will arrive early at Central Station
It has moved to a different platform
It will depart about twenty minutes late
items.explanation: The announcement gives a twenty-minute delay because of track work, so the train leaves about twenty minutes late and is not cancelled.

items.stem: A voicemail message says, "This is Dr. Alvarez's office calling to confirm your appointment tomorrow at 3 p.m. Please call us if you need to reschedule." What is the purpose of the call?
options: To offer a refund for treatment
To request payment of an old bill
items.explanation: The message confirms the time of an appointment and mentions rescheduling, so its purpose is confirmation, not sales, refunds or billing.

items.stem: An announcement reminds staff that expense claims must be submitted with receipts before the end of each month. What are staff reminded to do?
options: Send expense claims with receipts monthly
Keep receipts for a full year only
items.explanation: The reminder is to submit expense claims with receipts before each month ends, so the matching option is monthly submission with receipts.

items.stem: A photograph shows a delivery van parked beside a warehouse while a worker carries a parcel toward the open loading door. What is the worker doing?
options: Carrying a parcel into the warehouse
Reading a newspaper at a desk
items.explanation: The image shows the worker moving a parcel toward the open warehouse door, so the worker is carrying a parcel inside; the other actions are not depicted.

items.stem: In a photograph, a group of office workers sit around a table with laptops and coffee cups, looking at a shared screen. What are the workers doing?
items.explanation: The workers are seated around a table with devices and a shared screen, which depicts a meeting; the other options describe maintenance or shopping.

items.stem: A receptionist asks, "May I have your name and company, please?" Which response is the most appropriate?
options: It is Kenji Mori from Yamada Trading.
The elevator is out of order.
items.explanation: The receptionist requests a name and company, so the reply giving both answers; the others supply times or unrelated information.

items.stem: A colleague asks, "Have you finished the inventory count?" Which reply best answers the question?
options: The shelves are made of metal.
Let us have lunch at noon.
Nearly, I just have the last shelf left.
items.explanation: The question is a yes or no question about completion, so the reply reporting near completion answers it; the others are unrelated statements.

items.stem: A client asks, "When can we expect the proposal?" Which response is the most suitable?
options: We should have it ready by Wednesday.
I do not have a pen.
items.explanation: The client asks for a time, and the reply gives Wednesday, answering it; the others comment on cost or give irrelevant replies.

items.stem: In a conversation, an employee asks the IT desk why the printer on the third floor is not working, and the technician says a new part has been ordered. Why is the printer not working?
options: It has run out of paper
It is being moved to another floor
It is waiting for a replacement part
It was never connected to power
items.explanation: The technician says a new part was ordered, implying the printer awaits a replacement; paper, relocation and power are not mentioned.

items.stem: In a conversation, a manager asks an assistant to book a hotel near the airport for a two-day trade fair and to keep the cost under the budget. What does the manager want booked?
options: A restaurant for a birthday party
A conference room in the office
An affordable hotel close to the airport
A taxi to the train station
items.explanation: The request specifies a hotel near the airport within budget for a trade fair, so the matching option is an affordable hotel near the airport.

items.stem: In a conversation, a customer tells a bank clerk that a charge on the statement looks wrong, and the clerk says a dispute form must be completed. What does the clerk ask the customer to do?
options: Fill in a dispute form about the charge
items.explanation: The clerk's response to a disputed charge is to complete a dispute form, so that is the requested action; the other options are not requested.

items.stem: An announcement states, "Due to heavy snow, all outbound flights this evening will be delayed, and passengers should check the screens for updates." What should passengers do?
options: Leave the airport and return tomorrow
Check the screens for updated information
items.explanation: The announcement advises passengers to watch the screens for updates, so that is the recommended action; boarding normally contradicts the delay notice.

items.stem: A presentation says, "Our sales rose twelve per cent in the second quarter, driven mainly by strong demand in the northern region." What caused the sales increase?
options: Strong demand in the northern region
A rise in advertising in the south
items.explanation: The speaker attributes the twelve per cent rise mainly to strong northern demand, so that is the stated cause; the other factors are not named.

items.stem: An announcement welcomes guests to the Riverside Hotel and says breakfast is served from six thirty to ten in the Garden Restaurant on the first floor. Where is breakfast served?
options: In the Garden Restaurant on the first floor
items.explanation: The announcement names the Garden Restaurant on the first floor as the breakfast location, so the other locations are incorrect.

items.stem: A photograph shows two mechanics in overalls inspecting the engine of a car that is raised on a lift in a garage. What is being inspected?
options: A bicycle in a shop window
The engine of a car on a lift
A washing machine in a laundry
items.explanation: The image shows mechanics examining a raised car's engine, so that is the object of inspection; bicycles, aircraft and appliances are not shown.

items.stem: An office manager asks, "Who is taking minutes at today's meeting?" Which reply is the most appropriate?
options: I believe Sara is, as usual.
I do not own a watch.
items.explanation: The question asks who will take minutes, so naming Sara answers it; the other replies refer to room access, length or watches, which do not answer who.

items.stem: A traveller asks, "Is there a shuttle from the airport to the hotel?" Which response best answers the question?
options: Yes, it runs every thirty minutes.
items.explanation: The question asks whether a shuttle exists, so a yes reply with its frequency answers it; the others are unrelated facts.

items.stem: In a job interview, a candidate says she led a team of ten and reduced delivery delays by half. What is the candidate describing?
options: A hobby she enjoys at weekends
A complaint about her old manager
A request for a higher salary
An achievement from a previous role
items.explanation: Leading a team and cutting delays are work accomplishments, so the candidate is presenting an achievement; hobbies, complaints and salary are not described.

items.stem: An announcement says the elevator to the upper floors is out of service today and asks people to use the stairs or the elevator in the east wing. What is the problem?
options: The stairs are closed for repairs
One elevator is out of service
The east wing is being demolished
items.explanation: The notice says the elevator to the upper floors is out of service and directs people to alternatives, so one elevator is unavailable; the stairs and east wing elevator work.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "Please submit the signed contract _____ the end of the business day." Which word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: With a deadline such as the end of the business day, the preposition by means no later than, which fits; until implies continuation, and during and since do not mark a deadline.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "All employees must wear a security badge _____ entering the production area." Which word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: Before entering expresses an action that must precede entry, which matches a rule about badges; the other words do not fit the required sequence.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "The finance team submitted a _____ report on last quarter's spending." Which form of the word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: The noun report needs an adjective before it, and detailed is the adjective; detail and details are nouns and detailing is a verb form.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "Because raw materials became more expensive, the company decided to _____ production costs." Which word best fits?
items.explanation: Rising costs call for lowering them, and reduce means to lower, which fits; the other verbs do not relate to cutting costs.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "The manager, along with the sales staff, _____ attending the regional conference next week." Which verb form is correct?
items.explanation: The subject is the singular manager; the phrase along with the sales staff does not change the number, so the singular is agrees with it.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "Customers who receive a faulty item may _____ a full refund within fourteen days." Which word best fits?
items.explanation: A refund is asked for, so request fits; reject, retire and reside do not describe asking for a refund.

items.stem: A memo reads, "The new expense policy takes effect on Monday. Staff should submit claims _____ fifty dollars with a receipt." Which phrase best fills the blank?
items.explanation: The policy requires a receipt for claims above a threshold, so over fifty dollars fits; the other choices do not express an amount threshold.

items.stem: An email reads, "Thank you for your order. Your items will be shipped within two days, and a tracking number will be sent _____ ." Which phrase best fills the blank?
items.explanation: A tracking number is naturally sent separately by email, so that phrase completes the sentence; the other phrases are unrelated idioms of place and time.

items.stem: A notice reads, "The photocopier on the third floor is temporarily out of order. Please use the machine on the second floor _____ ." Which phrase best fills the blank?
items.explanation: Until further notice is the standard phrase for a temporary closure, so it completes the notice; the other phrases do not fit the context.

items.stem: A supplier's email says, "Our records show your last payment is overdue by thirty days. Please settle the balance this week to keep your account active." What does the supplier want?
items.explanation: The email asks the customer to settle an overdue balance to keep the account active, so it requests payment; the other options are not mentioned.

items.stem: A notice says the staff car park will be resurfaced from Monday to Wednesday and that employees should use the public car park on King Street. What should employees do from Monday to Wednesday?
options: Park at the public car park on King Street
Work from home for three days
Arrive before seven in the morning
Leave their cars at the front entrance
items.explanation: The notice redirects employees to the King Street public car park during resurfacing, so that is the required action.

items.stem: An advertisement says that Green Leaf Cafe is hiring part-time baristas, that no experience is required, and that full training is provided. What does the advertisement offer?
options: Training for a role that needs no experience
items.explanation: The advertisement says no experience is required and full training is provided, so it offers training for beginners; the other benefits are not stated.

items.stem: A workshop schedule runs from 9.00 to 12.00, breaks for lunch until 1.00, then continues with a practical session from 1.00 to 4.30. How long is the practical session?
items.explanation: The practical session runs from 1.00 to 4.30, which is three and a half hours; the other figures match other parts of the day.

items.stem: An invoice lists ten boxes of paper at eight dollars each, plus a delivery fee of twenty dollars. What is the total amount due?
items.explanation: Ten boxes at eight dollars is eighty dollars, plus the twenty dollar delivery fee, giving a total of one hundred dollars.

items.stem: A memo states that from next month all travel bookings must be approved by a department head before tickets are purchased. What is the new rule?
options: All travel is suspended next month
Employees may book whatever tickets they wish
Tickets must be purchased a month in advance
A department head must approve travel before tickets are bought
items.explanation: The memo requires a department head's approval before tickets are bought, so that is the new rule; it does not suspend travel or set a booking window.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "The customer asked _____ the warranty covered accidental damage." Which word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: An indirect question about coverage uses whether to introduce the clause; that, which and because do not fit the embedded question.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "To avoid delays, please _____ all boxes clearly with the destination address." Which word best fits?
items.explanation: Boxes are marked for shipping by labelling them, so label fits; the other words are unrelated in meaning.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "The company reported a significant _____ in online sales last year." Which form of the word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: After the adjective significant, a noun is required, and increase is the noun; the other forms are verb or adverb forms that do not fit.

items.stem: An email reads, "We have received your application and will contact you within five working days. Please do not reply to this message, as it is sent _____ ." Which phrase best fills the blank?
items.explanation: Automatically explains why the message should not be answered, which fits an automated confirmation; the other adverbs do not convey this meaning.

items.stem: A policy reads, "Employees should keep their passwords confidential and change them _____ ." Which phrase best fills the blank?
items.explanation: A password policy normally sets a regular interval such as every ninety days, which fits the blank; the other phrases are idioms with unrelated meanings.

items.stem: A client's email says, "Could we move our meeting from Tuesday to Thursday at the same time? I have an urgent appointment on Tuesday." Why does the client want to move the meeting?
options: The client has another appointment on Tuesday
The client prefers a different room
The client cannot find the office
The client wants a shorter meeting
items.explanation: The client cites an urgent appointment on Tuesday as the reason, so the meeting is moved because of a schedule clash; the other reasons are not given.

items.stem: A notice says that visitors must sign in at reception and wear a visitor badge at all times while on site. What must visitors do while on site?
options: Wear a visitor badge at all times
Sign in only when they leave
items.explanation: The notice requires visitors to wear a badge at all times on site, so that is the rule; signing in is on arrival, not only on leaving, and no uniform is required.

items.stem: A product description says the all-weather jacket is fully waterproof and includes a detachable hood, making it suitable for both city and mountain use. What feature does the jacket have?
items.explanation: The description names a detachable hood and waterproofing, so the detachable hood is the stated feature; the other features are not mentioned.

items.stem: A sales table shows Region A at 45 units, Region B at 30 units, Region C at 65 units, and Region D at 20 units. Which region sold the most units?
items.explanation: Region C is listed at 65 units, which is higher than the other three regions, so it sold the most.

items.stem: A customer writes, "I am writing to complain about a delay in delivery. My order was promised last Monday but arrived nine days later." What is the customer doing?
options: Thanking the company for fast service
Applying for a job with the company
items.explanation: The letter states its purpose as a complaint about a delivery that arrived nine days late, so the customer is complaining, not thanking or applying.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "By the time the auditors arrived, the accounts _____ already been reconciled." Which word best completes the sentence?
items.explanation: The past perfect had been reconciled describes an action completed before another past event; have and has are present-tense forms and having is not a finite verb here.

items.stem: An incomplete sentence reads, "The two departments agreed to _____ resources so that both could meet the deadline." Which word best fits?
items.explanation: Departments working together to meet a deadline would share resources, so share fits; the other verbs do not describe joint use of resources.

items.stem: A memo reads, "Due to a scheduled system upgrade, the online portal will be unavailable from 10 p.m. Friday to 2 a.m. Saturday. We apologise for any _____ ." Which word best fills the blank?
items.explanation: A service outage apology conventionally cites inconvenience, which fits the blank; the other nouns are unrelated to the context.

items.stem: A manager's email says, "Great news. The board has approved the new marketing budget, so we can begin the campaign in April as planned." What can now proceed?
items.explanation: Approval of the budget allows the marketing campaign to begin in April, so that is what can proceed; the other activities are not mentioned.

items.stem: A memo says that the helpdesk will operate reduced hours this holiday weekend, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. both days. What are the helpdesk's hours this weekend?
items.explanation: The memo gives reduced hours of 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on both days, so that is the schedule; the helpdesk is not closed all weekend.
